title: [Proposal] Applying builder pattern to RuntimeConfig
Band refactoring (Core / Interface)
body:
This PR contains the main core / interfaces that are not a simple migration.
Please note that the base of this PR is this branch (https://github.com/mrsnu/band/tree/band_refactor_base) with the following changes to remove irrelevant changes in this PR.
* current master band -> `tensorflow_band`
* TensorFlow lite 2.3.0 -> `TensorFlow`
* migrate utility / not implemented files (such as `cpu` and scheduler implementations)

There are two types of key changes depending on the main purpose.

### Key changes for the backend-agnostic framework
1. `Interface` classes define backend-agnostic interfaces. Each backend (e.g., Tensorflow Lite, MNN, ...) should implement these interfaces to communicate with the band core. 
2. `Model` corresponds to a unique DNN model for every backend. For example, a user should create a single `Band::Model` for mobilenet v2, and register each of the backend models (which inherits `Band::Interface::IModel`) before `Engine::RegisterModel` to create corresponding interpreters.
3. `Tensor` implements the band's own tensor type based on `Band::Interface::ITensor`. It communicates with a backend tensor with each of the backend tensor's view (that inherits `Band::Interface::ITensorView`).
4. `Interpreter` supports DNN execution for <worker, model> pair. This design could reduce the memory usage of some backend / device that supports subgraph execution. (e.g., TFLite OpenCL GPU delegate).
The above change requires global refactoring from an index-based subgraph handle to `SubgraphKey`.

### Key changes for dependency removal
1. `Context` class provides an interface for `scheduler`, `planner`, and `worker` classes. This design minimizes dependencies between core classes for ease of testing.
2. `Engine` class implements band core logic with actual classes and exposes user-facing APIs for multi- DNN inference.

### Additional changes to remove stateful code blocks
   * model registration steps in `InterpreterBuilder` 
   * scheduler only suggests a set of scheduling decisions based on given context and requests.

This PR contains minimal tests based on gtest/gmock, accessible with `test_band.sh` script.
This branch (https://github.com/mrsnu/band/tree/band_refactor_tfl_backend) contains an example backend implementation with tensorflow lite 2.3.0 with an end-to-end model-level test.

body: Handling slo values per job.

title: Handling SLO violation in LSF scheduler
body:
### Before
* SLO violation jobs are handled by the planner.
* SLO violation in the planner : `current time + expected latency of current subgraph > enqueue time + slo`

### Changed
* Handle SLO violation in LSF scheduler by setting state of violation jobs to `kTfLiteJobSLOViolation`.
* SLO violation in the LSF scheduler : `current time + shortest expected latency of the left part  > enqueue time + slo`
* Apply `schedule_window_size` in LSF scheduler.

title: Latency Estimation per Worker
body:
### Before
* Shared `profile_copy_computation_ratio` for all workers

### Changed
* Configurable `profile_copy_computation_ratio` per worker
* ex)
```json
{
    "profile_copy_computation_ratio": 1000,
    "workers": [
      {
        "device": "CPU",
        "num_threads": 1,
        "cpu_masks": "BIG",
        "profile_copy_computation_ratio": 10
      }
    ]
}
```

Note
* Estimated latency is proportional to `flops + input/output size * profile_copy_computation_ratio`.

title: FLOPS/InputOutput Tensor Size-based latency estimation
body:
### Before
* Estimate latency with the number of operators in the subgraph

### Changed
* Estimate latency with FLOPS and size of input/output tensors of the subgraph
  * FLOPS considers only Conv2D, DepthwiseConv2D, TransposeConv2D
  * Input/output tensors also contains weights and bias.
* Added new parameter `profile_copy_computation_ratio`.
  * Assume latency is proportional to `FLOPS + profile_copy_computation_ratio * input/output tensor size`.

### To do
* Support FLOPS calculation for other operators.

title: Implement HEFTScheduler
Reduce scheduling overhead in GetShortestLatency
body:
This PR adds a cache feature to `Interpreter::GetShortestLatency()` so that the scheduler doesn't have to do a long traversal through all possible subgraph paths every time, when retrieving the shortest latency.

The cache is the form of {model_id, resolved_tensors} --> {best_subgraph_idx, expected_latency (when start_time == 0)}.
Note that the cache isn't always usable at runtime because one or more devices may be busy, i.e. `device_waiting_time[device] > 0`. The best subgraph is dependent on the waiting times, so we can't just do a lookup on the cache at all times without checking the waiting times. This PR solves this issue by comparing `start_time` (a function param of `GetShortestLatency()`) with the device waiting times: if `start_time` is larger than all waiting times, then the situation is the same as if the device waiting times were all zero so it is safe to do a cache lookup.

Big thanks to @dostos for suggesting this cache idea, as well as finding a critical bug in a previous version of this PR.

One of the key benefits of frequency-based estimation over our baseline (exponential smoothing) is responsiveness to unexpected frequency drops and exponential smoothing fails to predict latency when the request interval is large (more than ~40ms for CPU / ~100ms for GPU).

title: Planner nits
body:
~This PR implements Least slack time scheduler.~

[Slack time](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/least-slack-time-lst-scheduling-algorithm-in-real-time-systems/) is defined as below:
```
Slack time = D - t - e
,where D = deadline, t = current time, e = execution time
```

Jobs with little slack time are scheduled first according to the implementation.
Also, for the cases where SLO is violated, I've added a simple reschedule mechanism. Why? Check the bullets below:
* Currently, the only two ways to invoke the planner are 1) when new jobs arrived and 2)when a device becomes available.
* Now, think of a situation where all devices are idle while no new jobs are arriving. If the scheduled job happens to violate the SLO and the job is not passed to the worker, then there is no way for the remaining jobs to be scheduled, meaning we need another way to invoke planning.

### NOTE
* The scheduler is expecting the requests to have SLO in its `Job` struct.
* The scheduling overhead is huge when there are lots of jobs in the queue. We must optimize it soon.

title: Planner with multiple schedulers
body:
This PR changes the overall planner structure for multi-level queue scheduling. (probably two-level scheduling for us)

### Major Changes
1. There is only one `Plan()` method now. Previously, `Plan()` methods are implemented for each planner, even though they have sharable code blocks. For instance, codes for updating device waiting time and codes for checking SLO violations can be shared with each other. 
https://github.com/mrsnu/tflite/blob/b36a92618791d88a1c83b4dd080bf27185c9e0c3/tensorflow/lite/planner/planner.cc#L358-L371
2. Introduce `scheduler` that decides which jobs go where when a queue is given. Now we have `fixed-device scheduler`, `round-robin scheduler`, and `shortest-expected-latency scheduler`. The scheduling logic is generally copied from the existing codes.
Later, we can implement some other schedulers (e.g., `least slack time first scheduler`).
* Scheduler
    * input: a queue with `Jobs`.
    * output: an action that specifies which Jobs go what devices.

### Workflow
1. Specify which schedulers to use. If multiple schedulers are specified, then multiple queues are generated. The `i`th scheduler is in charge of handling the `i`th queue. The following example is with 2 queues, each with the fixed-deviced scheduler.
```json
# config.json
"schedulers" : [0, 0]
...
"running_time_ms" : ...
```
2. `Queues` and `Schedulers` are generated during the initialization.
https://github.com/mrsnu/tflite/blob/b36a92618791d88a1c83b4dd080bf27185c9e0c3/tensorflow/lite/planner/planner.cc#L50-L64

3. For each iteration in `Plan()`, `Scheduler` decides an action, Jobs for each worker, and enqueues the jobs to the workers.
 https://github.com/mrsnu/tflite/blob/b36a92618791d88a1c83b4dd080bf27185c9e0c3/tensorflow/lite/planner/planner.cc#L365-L369

title: [refactoring] Planner Util
body:
### Changes 1
Add `JobQueue` typing and `SharableJobQueue` struct in `planner/util.h`.
* A `JobQueue` is the same as `std::deque<Job>`.
* A `SharableJobQueue` consists of a `JobQueue` and a mutex.

The reason for the change is to make the implementation of the multi-level queue planner convenient. To be specific, I just did not want to make a vector of `std::deque<Job>` and another vector of `<std::mutex>`.
